acceptance: The real-tmux integration tests (TestRealTmuxSandboxTerminalConfinement, TestRealTmux_BracketedMultilinePromptPreservesBytes) pass on a host with a load average several times its core count, or report a named skip-with-reason that the floor counts as not-run rather than a failure (red first under an artificial CPU hog)
The boot budget such a test waits on is derived from the same config the production REPL boot uses, not a wall-clock literal in the test

consumed.resolution: Duplicate of realtmux-bridge-tests-flake-under-package-parallel-load (same test, same 'REPL prompt never appeared' rc=80 under host load); this is its 4th and 5th sighting, during the route-stamps floor on 2026-09-30 at a 15-minute load average of 34.

fix: Find what bounds the fixture REPL's boot in these tests and make it follow the production boot budget (or a load-aware budget), so host load slows the test instead of failing it.
source: console, 2026-10-01: classified twice on 2026-09-30/10-01 (the comment-strip trial and the tool branch's floor), both rc=80 'REPL prompt never appeared' while the host load average was 34; both pass in 1.5s in isolation on the branch and on unchanged main
summary: TestRealTmuxSandboxTerminalConfinement failed twice with rc=80 (REPL prompt never appeared) during local floors run beside loop lanes and reviewers, at a 15-minute load average of 34, and passes in 1.5 s in isolation on both the branch under test and unchanged main. A floor failure that depends on host load looks like a defect in whatever change is being floored and costs a classification each time.
title: The real-tmux integration tests fail under host load instead of waiting longer
